# CIDRKit

> Subnet and CIDR arithmetic that runs in your browser, checked against Python's ipaddress field by field.

All calculations run in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

## Tools

- [Subnet Calculator](http://cidrkit.com/subnet-calculator/): Enter a CIDR block, a dotted mask, a wildcard mask or an address range and get every derived value. Collapses 50,000 CIDRs in 188 ms. Nothing you paste is uploaded.

## Key facts

- A /24 holds 256 addresses and 254 usable hosts; the network and broadcast addresses are the difference.
- A /31 has 2 usable hosts (RFC 3021, point-to-point) and a /32 has 1. Applying minus-two to either is wrong.
- IPv6 has no broadcast address, so the minus-two rule does not exist there.
- A wildcard (host) mask is the exact inverse of a netmask; both spellings describe the same block.
- A block of CIDRs can be collapsed only when two blocks are equal size, adjacent and aligned on the parent boundary. Checked against Python's ipaddress on 356 inputs.
